subject: English Language

questions.prompt: Which lesson began every school day? (A English, B Science, C Mathematics, D Civic, E Health)
steps: The included page 6 script says the day begins with mathematics.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: What was life in class like? (A happy, B entertaining, C lazy, D risky, E interesting)
steps: The script describes falling walls and a pupil hit by a brick.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: How many mathematics lessons were there daily? (A one, B two, C three, D four, E five)
steps: The script states two mathematics lessons every day.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: How many pupils were in the class? (A 25, B 35, C 15, D 5, E 45)
steps: The script gives forty-five pupils.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Which teachers did pupils like? (A lazy/talkative, B good/hardworking, C tall/kind/humble, D cruel/hardworking, E poor/tall/humble)
steps: These exact qualities appear in the script.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Have you ___ your homework? (A finish, B finished, C finishing, D finishes, E will finish)
steps: Have requires the past participle finished.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Our teacher ___ come tomorrow. (A will, B shall, C is, D had, E was)
steps: Tomorrow indicates a future event.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: A. Will is the usual future form; shall is possible in formal determination.

questions.prompt: Choose a simple-present sentence. (A she went, B she has gone, C she goes every day, D she is going now, E she will go)
steps: Goes expresses a regular present habit.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: C. She goes to school every day.

questions.prompt: ___ our parents go to market yesterday? (A do, B does, C had, D have, E did)
steps: A simple-past question uses did plus base verb go.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Does Doreen ___ English daily? (A speak, B speaks, C speaking, D spoken, E spoke)
steps: Does takes the base verb.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: They have studied here ___ 2019. (for, since, in, at)
steps: Since introduces the starting year.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Choose ___ playing netball ___ resting. (either/or, neither/nor, both/and)
steps: Choosing between alternatives uses either...or.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Father bought the red car ___ the black ones. (besides, beside, with)
steps: Besides expresses an additional purchase, whereas beside locates the car and with can link purchases.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: Besides (intended: in addition to); beside/with allow different meanings.

questions.prompt: Yesterday ___ night pupils washed utensils. (in, on, at, of)
steps: At night is the fixed phrase; yesterday at night is less idiomatic than last night.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: At; natural corrected wording: last night.

questions.prompt: This is the son ___ father had an accident. (who, whose, whom, which)
steps: Whose shows possession of father.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Match library: A directions, B same-class person, C written information, D room/building with books, E eyewitness, F important invited person, G crowd, H shaking in fear.
steps: A library houses a collection of books.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: D. A building or room containing books.

questions.prompt: Match classmate.
steps: Classmate identifies a fellow member of one's class.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: B. A person in the same class as you.

questions.prompt: Match witness.
steps: A witness observes an event.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: E. A person who sees something happening.

questions.prompt: Match instructions.
steps: Instructions give directions.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: A. Words telling you what to do and how.

questions.prompt: Match guest of honour.
steps: The guest is specially honoured.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: F. The most important person invited to an event.

questions.prompt: Washel is the son of my aunt. He is my ___.
steps: Your aunt's child is your cousin.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Who sells fish at the market?
steps: A fishmonger sells fish; a fisherman catches fish.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: What is a place where meat is sold called?
steps: The place selling meat is a butcher's shop.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Write the plural of child.
steps: This is an irregular plural.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Write the opposite of sell.
steps: Buying and selling are opposite sides of a transaction.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: When did Salma and Prince travel to Mtongani?
steps: The opening gives the period of their visit.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Where did they live with their parents?
steps: The first sentence names the home district.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: What were the monkeys doing when the children saw them? (question prints Salma and Pendo)
steps: The passage states this action; Prince is the second child's name in the story.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: Jumping from one tree to another.

questions.prompt: Who cooked for the children at Mtongani?
steps: The final paragraph identifies the cook.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Which river did the bus cross?
steps: The second paragraph names it.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Order with A-E: She saw wild animals, hills and valleys along the road.
steps: This observation follows taking a window seat.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Order: On the bus she sat near the window.
steps: She boards after waking early.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Order: On the travelling day she woke early to catch the bus.
steps: The early start follows introduction of the visit.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Order: Last year Catherine visited her father in Mtwara.
steps: Introduce the traveller, purpose and destination first.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Order: She reached her father's home safely.
steps: Arrival completes the journey.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

summaries.Listening and grammar: Listen to the supplied teacher text and identify the exact detail asked for. Check spelling and sentence punctuation; missing scripts are explicitly identified.
summaries.Vocabulary: Use sentence meaning, subject agreement and time clues to choose the word or verb form. Apply the specific rule explained for each task and note ambiguous choices.
summaries.Comprehension and composition: Find evidence in the passage or poem before answering. Distinguish explicit statements, reasonable inferences and model interpretations.

references.title: SPES Standard Five 5 Monthly Exams September 2024

limitations: 3(iii): Besides is the intended addition meaning, but other printed prepositions have grammatical interpretations.
6(iii): Question changes Prince to Pendo; answer uses the passage event.
